उत्तराखंड में दिन-रात के तापमान में दोगुना अंतर, 23 अक्टूबर से बदलेगा मौसम का मिजाज
उत्तराखंड में मौसम शुष्क बना हुआ है, जहां दिन में धूप और रात में ठंडक महसूस हो रही है, जिससे ...और पढ़ें
समय कम है?
जानिए मुख्य बातें और खबर का सार एक नजर में
जागरण संवाददाता, देहरादून। उत्तराखंड में मौसम शुष्क बना हुआ है। पहाड़ से मैदान तक दिनभर चटख धूप खिलने से दिन में गर्मी का एहसास हो रहा है, जबकि सुबह और शाम ठंड बढ़ने लगी है। न्यूनतम तापमान में लगातार गिरावट के चलते मौसम में ठंडक घुलने लगी है।
मौसम विभाग के अनुसार, आज प्रदेश के सभी जनपदों में मौसम शुष्क रहने की संभावना है। प्रदेश में इन दिनों दिन और रात के तापमान में काफी अंतर देखने को मिल रहा है। दिन में धूप के कारण गर्मी महसूस हो रही है, वहीं सूर्यास्त के बाद हवा चलने से ठंडक बढ़ जाती है।
सुबह के समय भी तापमान में गिरावट का असर महसूस किया जा रहा है। ऐसे में लोगों को दिन में गर्मी और सुबह-शाम हल्की ठंड का सामना करना पड़ रहा है। मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, अगले कुछ दिनों तक प्रदेश में मौसम का मिजाज इसी तरह बना रह सकता है।
फिलहाल बारिश की संभावना कम है और अधिकांश क्षेत्रों में मौसम शुष्क रहने के आसार हैं। हालांकि, आगामी 23 अक्टूबर से प्रदेश के मौसम में बदलाव देखने को मिल सकता है। पश्चिमी विक्षोभ के सक्रिय होने के चलते पर्वतीय क्षेत्रों में मौसम करवट बदल सकता है। इससे पहाड़ी इलाकों में बादल छाने और मौसम में बदलाव की संभावना है।

Orange Alert: Chengalpet Collector Asks Officials To Keep Machinery Ready For Rescue Operations
The department said a total of about 4.15 lakh passengers have left by government buses to their native places in the last three days till Saturday.
Chennai: Chengalpet district Collector M. Veerappan inspected the Disaster Management Control room following an orange alert for the district and asked the officials keep all the arrangements including the machines and other equipment for rescue operations ready at the coastal taluks besides instructing them to monitor the complaints received in the control room.
The Collector who visited the control room on Saturday evening asked the Revenue department and fire station officials to be on their toes. The district received between 60 mm to 20 mm at various places and the heaviest rainfall of 60 mm was reported in Chengalpet taluk while Cheyyur recorded 50 mm while Tambaram received 46 mm.
There were no reports of damage to houses, cattle and human loss due to the rains on Saturday, according to the Collector’s office. A rainfall below 60 mm is considered moderate and falls under the dark green category, but the forecast of an orange alert indicates a warning for 115 mm to 204 mm.
The road in front of Kilambakkam terminus was inundated during the rains, but it was clear by Sunday. The transport department shifted the temporary bus stands for Ayudha Pooja from the climate park near the terminus and Maraimalai Nagar back to the usual platform inside the terminus as the number of passengers was not high on Sunday. The department said a total of about 4.15 lakh passengers have left by government buses to their native places in the last three days till Saturday.
The farmers had much to cheer for since the lakes started receiving water due to the rains. Of the 528 lakes maintained by the Water Resources Department in Chengalpet, the storage of one lake crossed 50 per cent while 117 of them crossed the 25 per cent storage, according to the executive engineer of the Water Resources Department. The water level in 408 lakes was less than 25 per cent since the initial rains were absorbed by the ground.
Among the 584 tanks under the maintenance of the Rural Development and Panchayat Raj department, two had crossed the 50 per cent storage mark and 99 of them have a storage of above 25 per cent while the storage is less than 25 per cent in 483 tanks. Besides, there are 2,512 ponds in the district and 8 of them had reached the 50 per cent storage level. The storage in 286 ponds is above 25 per cent while it is less than 25 per cent in 2,218 ponds. An orange alert means heavy rains and increase in the storage of the lakes and ponds.

Red alert in Chennai after extreme rainfall, flooding in several areas
As Chennai faces record rainfall, coordinated relief and preparedness measures highlight the city’s ongoing struggle to adapt to severe monsoon
Chennai, one of India’s largest metropolitan regions with over 8.6 million residents, is currently under a red alert due to extremely heavy rainfall predicted during the northeast monsoon season. The Regional Meteorological Centre in Chennai has forecast over 20 cm of rain in a 24-hour period starting Sunday afternoon.
Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Chennai also issued an orange alert for neighbouring Chengalpattu, Kancheepuram and Thiruvallur districts and western districts of Nilgiris, Coimbatore and Theni district in the same period.
This surge in precipitation is part of the active northeast monsoon impacting Tamil Nadu and adjacent regions.
As per reports, Parry’s Corner in Chennai received 36 cm of rain within 24 hours, with significant downpours also recorded in surrounding localities. The Greater Chennai Corporation said despite these intense weather conditions, authorities claimed all 22 subways had been cleared of waterlogging and National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF) teams have helped keep the situation under control with no major casualties reported so far.
The heavy rains recall the city’s vulnerability highlighted during historic floods such as those in 2015, which impacted over four million people and exposed critical gaps in preparedness. At that time, floodwaters disrupted daily life, closed schools, and paralysed industrial centres, underscoring Chennai’s rapid urban growth coupled with inadequate drainage and disaster management strategies. Since then, lessons learned have driven efforts to improve resilience but challenges remain significant given the increasing frequency and severity of monsoon-driven flooding tied to climate variability.
Meanwhile, Chief Minister Joseph Vijay reviewed relief efforts and flood-prevention measures at the Integrated State Command and Control Centre in the GCC's Ripon Building.
He instructed officials to inspect areas that had experienced waterlogging in the past and step up preventive works to avoid a recurrence, official sources said.
He also asked all departments to maintain strict coordination and execute relief measures diligently in anticipation of further heavy rain warnings, the sources added.
